title: feat(enter): expose BYOP app details from GET /account/key
author: davealan74
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #10733

## Changes

- **`enter.pollinations.ai/src/routes/account.ts`**: Replaces the flat `byopClientKeyId` field on `GET /account/key` with a `byopApp` object (`clientKeyId`, `name`, `appUser`) for BYOP-minted keys; `byopApp: null` for non-BYOP keys. Updates the OpenAPI schema accordingly. No new DB query — all three fields (`byopClientKeyId`, `byopClientName`, `byopClientUserId`) are already loaded by the auth middleware via a left-join on the BYOP client key.
- **`enter.pollinations.ai/test/account-key.test.ts`**: Updates the agent-run-token test to assert `byopApp: null` (non-BYOP parent key). Adds a dedicated test verifying `byopApp: null` for regular secret keys.

## Acceptance criteria

- Adds `byopApp` object to `GET /account/key` for BYOP-minted keys
- Includes `clientKeyId` (public app key/client id), `name` (app name), and `appUser` (app user identity)
- Field naming avoids `owner`; uses `appUser`
- Non-BYOP keys return `byopApp: null`
- Reuses fields already loaded by auth middleware — no new route query

gist.headline: Keys Know Their Garden
gist.blurb: BYOP-minted keys can now introduce the app that grew them. The account endpoint brings along the app name, client key, and app user—no extra database expedition required.
gist.summary: GET /account/key now returns a byopApp object for BYOP-minted keys with clientKeyId, name, and appUser, while regular and non-BYOP keys return byopApp: null.
gist.impact: BYOP developers can identify the originating app and app-user identity for a key from one account lookup, with a consistent null value for keys outside BYOP.
gist.visual_concept: Polli is tending a small garden of labeled API keys, with one key blooming into a tiny app placard showing its client ID, app name, and user badge. A friendly CRT monitor robot reads the key's new app-details card while ordinary keys rest beside clear "null" signposts, making the distinction feel organized rather than ominous.
